- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply “early bias correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.0% from first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment turns bearish, forecast should slope downward).
